meta.title: From the Station to the Museum

paragraphs: From the Station to the Museum, a route by Mia. Many visitors come to our town by train, and they want to see the science museum. Leo and I walked the route three times. We drew a map with a blue dashed line. Teacher Kim checked the route on a Saturday morning. This post gives you directions. Is the walk easy?

First, leave the station and turn right. Walk along the big road until you see the market. This part takes fifteen minutes. Use the crossing in front of the market, because the road is busy. Then turn down the side street. The side street has trees on both sides, so it is cool in the morning. The market has an orange circle on the map.

Next, continue down the side street for fifteen minutes. The town library is on your right, and it has a blue star on the map. The museum is at the end of the street, on your left. It has a green triangle on the map. The whole walk takes exactly thirty minutes at a normal speed. You can also take a taxi, but a taxi costs more than a bus.

Sometimes a train has a delay, so look at the board in the station. Leo says that delays are usually short, but I always bring a book. If the train is late, do not run. The museum is open until four o'clock. The last bus leaves the museum for the station at half past four. A bus ticket costs ten baht, and you can use it to return to the station. Keep your ticket in your bag, and do not lose it.

The museum has a surprising room about memory. Guide Ann gives each visitor a card with a picture. The room is dark, so you must stand still for a minute. You look at the card for one minute, and then you look at the wall. Many pictures shine on the wall, and you must find your picture. My memory is not good, so I lost the game. Leo has a good memory, and he won three times.
Please walk carefully, and keep to the side of the road. I think the memory room is the best part of the museum. Which part of the route do you like most? Tell us in a comment!
